title: Establish Retry Governor & Hedged-Request Contract for Inference SDKs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Context: Multiple Redwood services and language SDKs currently implement bespoke retry, timeout, and backoff behavior. Differences in default timeouts, backoff curves, idempotency handling, and hedged request semantics have caused SLO violations during multi-region failover and complicated debugging for customers. This ticket defines a single, backwards-compatible contract (the Retry Governor) and hedged-request extension that all services and SDKs will adopt.
goals: Define a single Retry Governor contract (headers + semantics) that standardizes retries, deadlines, backoff, and idempotency across services and SDKs
Provide a hedged-requests opt-in extension to reduce tail latency for inference calls while preserving at-most-once semantics via idempotency keys
Align retry behavior with SLOs and multi-region failover policies so client-side retries do not interfere with server-side load shedding and circuit-breakers
Ship SDK changes for JS, Python, and Go with feature flags and clear backwards compatibility guarantees
Add telemetry and dashboards to measure retry volume, hedged request incidence, and outage amplification
non_goals: Rewriting every service's internal circuit-breaker implementation (we will integrate via published signals)
Enforcing idempotency on arbitrary non-idempotent user payloads — we only standardize metadata and guidance
Large-scale migration of legacy SDKs in this sprint (we will provide adapters and deprecation schedule)
proposed_contract_summary: Server and client agree on a small set of headers and parameters. Clients send: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key, X-Redwood-Retry-Mode (standard|hedged), X-Redwood-Retry-Governor (json-safe policy token), X-Redwood-Client-Deadline-ms. Servers respond with Retry-Allowed, Retry-After-ms, and Hedged-Decision headers. The server may override client hints and will emit telemetry when it rejects retries due to load shedding.
compatibility_notes: Default behavior stays the same for existing SDKs unless the new global config is enabled. Hedged requests are opt-in per call and disabled by default. Idempotency header is optional but required to enable safe hedging for mutating endpoints. There will be an adapter layer in the API gateway to translate legacy retry headers into the new contract for incremental rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc merged to Confluence with example request/response traces
JS/Python/Go SDKs implement Retry Governor defaults behind a feature flag and include automated tests that assert idempotency key generation and hedging opt-in
Gateway PR adds header passthrough and a lightweight adapter for legacy clients (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1342)
Dashboards: retry-rate, hedged-rate, amplification-rate, and retry-rejections added to console with alert thresholds
Runbook updated: steps for toggling hedging, circuit-breaker thresholds to tune alongside retries, and rollback actions
plan: Phase 1 (week 1): Draft contract and example SDK API; internal review with Runtime, SDK, and SRE teams (owner: Liam)
Phase 2 (week 2): Implement feature-flagged SDK support + gateway adapter; unit tests and e2e harness (owner: Priya)
Phase 3 (week 3): Shape observability (traces/metrics) and dashboard panels; run chaos test for multi-region failover (owner: SRE)
Phase 4 (week 4): Beta with a handful of internal services and one customer workload; gather metrics and iterate (owner: product)
Phase 5 (post-beta): Gradual rollout and deprecation schedule for legacy retry headers
risks_and_tradeoffs: Client complexity: providing hedging and idempotency helpers in SDKs adds surface area — mitigated by high-quality defaults and examples
Amplified failures: badly-configured retries/hedging can amplify load during partial outage — mitigated by server-side enforcement, circuit-breaker signals, and conservative defaults
Backward compatibility: adapter layer increases gateway complexity but enables incremental rollout
Observability gaps: we must ensure request-level trace ids survive retries and hedges to avoid double-counting
implementation_notes: Default backoff: jittered exponential: base=50ms, factor=2.0, max_backoff=5s, max_retries=3 for idempotent calls (tunable by Governor token)
Deadline propagation: clients must send X-Redwood-Client-Deadline-ms and SDKs should cap cumulative retry time to 70% of that value to leave room for server processing

Hedging semantics: when X-Redwood-Retry-Mode=hedged and an idempotency key is present, client may issue a single parallel hedged attempt at 180ms after initial request for generation calls; server responds with Hedged-Decision to indicate which attempt won
Server signals: services will return Retry-Allowed=false when load-shedding or circuit-breakers active; SDKs should surface retry rejections as a distinct metric
Audit: all hedged or retried requests will include original request-id and attempted-sequence to maintain trace continuity
